Cc: sophie.clarke@lythiahealth.com
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Lythia VPC — sudden QPS surge, 5xx increase

Hi Rachel / Redwood,

We just observed an abrupt QPS spike from our ingestion fleet starting ~07:50 PDT that has driven p95 latency from ~180ms to ~1.5s and 5xx rate up to ~7% on calls routed to our private VPC deployment. This is user-facing for a significant portion of sessions (estimated 18% of traffic).

We're on the Lythia private deployment (cluster: lythia-prod-vpc-3). Attached: trace log and a small snapshot of request headers. The timing coincides with a scheduled batch ingest from one of our partners, but the request shape changed (many small concurrent requests instead of batched requests) so it's likely a pattern change.

Can you confirm whether this looks like a runtime/backpressure issue vs. something client-side? We're starting to see client retries amplify traffic. Sophie (cc) is standing by for exec updates.

Alex Turner
SRE, Lythia Health

Alex — thanks for the signal and for the artifacts. We've triaged the first pass and will treat as an urgent operational incident. Immediate plan (next 45 minutes):

- Triage: our on-call will pull a full KV/cache+accept-queue snapshot and CPU/GPU utilization for the Lythia cluster. Requesting you keep the trace attached alive for 2 hours.
- Short-term mitigations: enable per-route burst capacity (temporary) and flip traffic for the heaviest route to a quantized variant (m1-small-8q) to reduce per-token time.
- Customer protection: advise you to throttle partner ingestion to 60% for the next 30 minutes if possible to reduce retry amplification.
- Exec sync: propose a 14:00 PT call today for a brief (15 min) with Sophie and Lythia leadership to review impact and next steps — is that OK?

Laura and Marissa — looping you in to own runtime tuning and rollback plan. Jonas, I'll escalate to you if we need leadership coordination.

I'll post running updates in #ops-urgent and attach a diagnostic collection guide for your team to run (small script) if you can execute it.

Regards,
Rachel Kim

Subject: Re: Lythia VPC — initial analysis and quick fixes

Thanks Rachel — quick summary from the runtime side after a first-pass on the trace and the limited metrics Alex sent:

- Symptom set: sudden spike to ~9k concurrent request attempts across the cluster, high small-payload concurrency (many < 60 token requests), accept-queue depth hit configured max, KV cache churn increased leading to higher cache miss rates and extra token decoding work.
- Immediate cause hypothesis: request shape changed (parallel small requests) exposing request scheduling and worker-thread contention in our VPC runtime path. This manifests as higher syscall/backpressure and transient 502/504s as accept queue overflows.

Immediate actions taken (done or in-progress):
1) Increased per-node concurrency cap from 24 -> 48 (temporary) to relieve accept-queue pressure.
2) Enabled per-route burst multiplier (x2) for the top-5 Lythia routes to allow short bursts while we stabilize.
3) Flipped routing for /embed and /short-gen to model variant m1-small-8q (quantized) to lower per-token latency.
4) Purged prefix cache entries for the tenant to reduce cache churn and allow a cold rebuild in a controlled window.

Early results: p95 dropped from ~1.5s to ~260ms within ~18 minutes of the config changes; 5xx rate down to ~0.6%. We are still monitoring; CPU and GPU utilization remain below emergency thresholds but network socket queues are a bit elevated.

Next recommended items (for a 2–4 hour window):
- Schedule a short maintenance window to raise worker threads + tune accept-queue thresholds permanently for tenant (post-incident).
- Add a targeted rate-limit rule on the partner ingestion path to avoid future amplification.
- Run a focused load test with partner payload (mimic small, highly concurrent requests) to validate the new knobs.

I'll keep the Lythia team posted. If leadership wants a one-slide summary for the 14:00 PT sync, I can draft quickly.

Laura Bennett
Head of Platform Operations, Redwood Inference

Quick status update and exec-friendly summary for Sophie's call:

- Timeline: incident detected 07:50 PT, mitigation toggles applied by 08:05-08:30 PT, measurable recovery by ~08:48 PT.
- Impact: ~18% of live sessions affected at peak; p95 improved from ~1.5s -> ~240-300ms; 5xx reduced from 7% -> ~0.6%.
- Root-cause (working hypothesis): traffic-shape change from partner ingestion producing many small concurrent requests exposing scheduler/accept-queue limits in the private runtime; not a model regression.

Actions taken (completed):
- Raised per-node concurrency cap temporarily.
- Enabled per-route burst and routed heavy paths to quantized model variants to reduce per-token compute.
- Purged tenant prefix cache and initiated controlled rebuild.

Pending (next 24 hours):
- Permanent tuning plan: increase worker threads + adjust accept queue sizing per node for Lythia cluster; validate with partner load test.
- Follow-up: customer readiness doc + configuration change schedule (we will own).
